findings.title: Unpacked reserved subscript assignment targets become plain evidence
findings.detail: A reserved dictionary subscript in a tuple or list assignment target can be followed by a comma and another target before equals. The classifier requires the closing target bracket/parentheses to lead directly to an assignment or colon and misses this valid write. Four bounded forms cover tuple-first, list, nested tuple and starred remainder targets. Static AST Store-target inspection confirms the reserved literal keys without executing input. Both classifiers return None in all 96 pairs across eight UTF encoding views and plain/gzip/XZ recovery. Sixty actual temporary working-file plain reads return these bytes across UTF8/16/32 and five suffixes. Shared exact-revision read and recovered-payload branches use the same classifier; synthetic bound-read fixtures were not created. This establishes a metadata classification boundary defect, without asserting a complete task PASS forgery. S9 comment-separated target repairs reject in all eight reviewed forms.
findings.required_change: Conservatively recognize reserved writes within unpacked assignment targets while preserving equivalent ordinary tuple/list reader expressions. Do not execute input, trust source syntax or relax binding/history/suffix guards. Add focused shared plain/recovery/history/suffix regressions and obtain fresh exact-revision review.
